comments.author: user-curator
comments.body: HB-14's comment window is open. The Ridgeline Act doesn't split along the usual lines — it's less ridge-vs-river than everyone weighing towers, jobs, air, and cost differently. If you could change one thing to make this bill better, what is it?

comments.author: cit-maziek
comments.body: Front-load the transition fund. We've heard 'retraining' before and got a brochure. Show me Title III is funded before a single tower goes up and Iron Ridge can live with the rest.

comments.author: cit-nonewtaxesned
comments.body: Translation: another Watauga slush fund with our names on the invoice. Hard pass.
comments.note: Snark that the floor de-amplifies (low bridge, no cross-stance endorsement). Civil-enough to stay visible; not the flagged F1 fixture.

comments.author: cit-ridgelinerose
comments.body: I've walked these ridges my whole life and the towers will hurt to see. I've also read Title I's setbacks and lived through three bad fire seasons. I'm genuinely torn.

comments.author: cit-twokidstwoinhalers
comments.body: Both my kids carry inhalers up here. Whatever the towers cost the view, I'll pay it for a clear breath.

comments.author: cit-clerkemeritus
comments.body: I'll never love the towers on our ridge. But read Title IV. Cap the ratepayer cost the way Okafor wants, fund the plateau's retraining FIRST, and only then build. That isn't a Watauga bill or a plateau bill — it's the compromise already written into the text, and both sides are arguing past it.
comments.note: The exemplar. Authored high bridge: balanced cross-stance endorsement (Homestead + Headwaters), high valuable_rate. The pipeline seeds these authored values directly on the comment row (display-only; the live scorer never computes synthetic).

comments.author: cit-plateaupride
comments.body: I came here to argue. But this is the first version of 'transition' that puts us first in line instead of last. If it's funded first, I can sell that at home.

comments.author: cit-oldgrowthowen
comments.body: A conservationist and a coal town agreeing on the sequencing — that's the bill working. Cap it, fund them first, build it right.

comments.author: cit-ridgelinerose
comments.body: Alright. Fund-first plus the Title I setbacks, and I can carry this to the trail association without feeling like a sellout.

comments.author: cit-plateaupride
comments.body: Coal built these towns and fed my family for three generations. I'm not against the future. I'm against being told my whole past was a mistake.
